summary: A one-off ticketed art benefit at A-B Tech's Ivy Building selling artwork to raise money to renovate the historic farmhouse on the Smith Farmstead at Bailey Mountain Preserve in Mars Hill, NC, described as being 'for the Appalachian Barn Alliance.' The listing gives no organizer contact, membership language, or link for the Alliance itself; it reads as a beneficiary of the fundraiser rather than the event's host (A-B Tech Ivy Building is listed as organizer).

evidence.note: Both listings describe only a single ticketed opening-night art sale with food/wine/beer to raise renovation funds for a specific farmhouse; no mention of members, meetings, dues, volunteers, or how to join the Alliance.
Organizer field is 'A-B Tech Ivy Building', not the Alliance itself, suggesting the college venue is running the benefit on the Alliance's behalf rather than the Alliance running a recurring event.

Bing and DuckDuckGo searches for 'Appalachian Barn Alliance' returned no website, Facebook page, Meetup, or news coverage of any organization by this name; searches for the Smith Farmstead / Bailey Mountain Preserve barn project also turned up nothing relevant.

Historic-barn preservation 'alliances' exist as real membership nonprofits in several states (e.g. Ohio, Indiana, Pennsylvania barn alliances) with dues-paying members, tours, and volunteer restoration work, so the name pattern is plausible for a genuine civic/advocacy group even though this specific one could not be corroborated online.
